questions.q: Why can creating new features improve a model even when no new data is collected?
options: It reshapes existing information into forms that make the pattern easier for the algorithm to learn
It increases the number of rows in the training set
It removes the need for a validation set
It guarantees the model will never overfit
questions.explain: Feature engineering rearranges information you already have, such as ratios or date parts, so the signal is easier to learn. It doesn't add rows or guarantee anything.

questions.q: An orders table has total and items columns. Which new feature is a ratio that may carry a signal neither column shows alone?
options: total + items
total / items, the average item price
items squared only
The row index
questions.explain: Dividing the order total by the item count gives the average item price, a behavior signal that isn't visible in either raw column alone.

questions.q: Why apply np.log1p to a right-skewed column such as income?
options: It converts the column to categories
It removes all missing values
It compresses the long tail, and it stays safe when a value is zero
It makes the column unique per row
questions.explain: A log transform compresses very large values so they don't dominate the scale. log1p computes log(1 + x), which is defined even when x is zero.

questions.q: Which engineered feature would leak the future and should be avoided?
options: Month extracted from the order date
Average item price for the current order
Days since the customer's previous purchase before this order
Total refunds issued in the year after the order, when predicting at order time
questions.explain: Refunds issued after the order would not be known when the prediction is made. That is data leakage. The other three use only information available at prediction time.

questions.q: You bin income into low, mid, and high using edges you chose by looking at the whole dataset's quantiles. What is the safest practice?
options: Compute quantile-based edges on the training split only, then apply them to validation and test
Compute edges on the test set so they match it exactly
Recompute edges separately for every split
Skip validation because binning can't hurt
questions.explain: Anything learned from data, like bin edges from quantiles, should be fit on the training split and then applied unchanged to the other splits. Otherwise information leaks.
